items.title: Governing Delegation to Generative Artificial Intelligence: Human Direction, Work-Related Orientation, and Modes of Use
items.desc: Distinguishes two ways humans retain direction when delegating cognitive work to generative AI — specified delegation (instructions set before execution) versus iterative coproduction (correcting outputs during production). Uses aggregate monthly cells from the Anthropic Economic Index for April–May 2026 to test whether more work-oriented interaction is associated with more specified delegation across API and consumer modes of use. [arXiv cs.CY, econ.GN, posted 2026-08-18]

items.title: Stranded credentials: how a skill-signaling market absorbed generative AI
items.desc: Audits the 2010–2026 Kaggle archive (444,698 participations) to ask whether competition medals still predict later performance in the generative-AI era. Fresh medals retain most of their signaling value, but stocks of older upload-competition medals lost roughly 82% of their informativeness — credentials are only as informative as their replenishment. [arXiv econ.GN, submitted 2026-08-17, announced 2026-08-19]

items.title: Communicating Credit Risk with Large Language Models: Evaluation of Explanations from Standard and Alternative Data-Based Models
items.desc: Tests whether LLMs can act as an explanation layer that turns technical credit-model outputs (XGBoost+SHAP, GNN+GNNExplainer, and a bimodal tabular-plus-network pipeline on Freddie Mac loan-level data) into risk narratives stakeholders can actually use. Compares three LLM configurations on the quality and fidelity of the resulting explanations. [arXiv q-fin.RM, cs.AI, posted 2026-08-18]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: An A.I. Tax Boom Could Curtail America's Debt. But Not Solve It.
items.desc: A growing number of economists expect widespread AI adoption to raise productivity and growth, and with it federal tax revenue, structurally narrowing the US deficit — provided AI does not displace too many workers. Gross debt, now around $40 trillion, would still grow, just more slowly. [NYT, published 2026-08-18]

items.title: Chinese Robot Maker Unitree Soars 500 Percent in Trading Debut
items.desc: Unitree Robotics rose almost 500% on its Shanghai debut, reaching roughly a $53 billion valuation after pricing its IPO at about a $9 billion valuation earlier in the month. Analysts quoted in the piece attribute much of the move to speculative enthusiasm for frontier AI and humanoid robotics. [NYT, published 2026-08-18]

items.title: How New York Is Restricting Data Centers
items.desc: New York has become one of the most aggressive states in regulating the hyperscale data centers underpinning AI, with Gov. Kathy Hochul imposing a first-in-the-nation one-year moratorium on state approvals amid concerns about electricity demand. [NYT, published 2026-08-18]

items.title: Young Americans really hate AI. These two charts show how much.
items.desc: A new Pew survey finds 52% of US adults are more concerned than excited about AI in daily life, up from about 38% in late 2022, and for the first time a majority of under-30s are in that camp — with a rising share expecting AI to destroy jobs. [Washington Post, published 2026-08-18]

items.title: AI triggers a wave of anxiety among the world's greatest math minds
items.desc: Research mathematicians are debating what remains distinctly human as AI systems become capable of doing original mathematical research — a case study in how rapidly AI is encroaching on elite knowledge work. [Washington Post, published 2026-08-19]

items.title: Does AI stop children from learning?
items.desc: A data-led look at the evidence on whether AI tools help or hinder learning outcomes for schoolchildren — relevant to the human-capital channel that most macro estimates of AI's growth effects depend on. [The Economist, published 2026-08-18]
